_note: The brief asked for a top-level array PLUS a `section2019` key. JSON cannot hold both, so the array lives under `items` and `section2019` sits beside it. Every `printedStem`/`options` value below is a verbatim transcription of the rendered page image (these PDFs are scans with no usable text layer); nothing has been repaired. All PNGs cited are in scripts/mh-hsc-12-pyq/out/verify2/.

items.printedStem: The principal solutions of \(\sec x = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) are
items.ourVersionWrong: Option D only. We hold D as "pi/6, 11pi/6", byte-identical to B. The paper prints D as \(\dfrac{\pi}{6},\ \dfrac{11\pi}{4}\) -- the second term is 11pi/4, not 11pi/6. A, B and C are faithful. The four printed options are all distinct, so there is no duplicate on the page. B is the only option carrying the correct value pi/6, 11pi/6, so the key is B.
items.source: Maths 2018 paper.pdf, page index 0, Q.1(A) ii; crop y 0.455-0.565 x 0.08-0.72 @120dpi (q1_2018_ii.png)

items.printedStem: In \(\Delta\) ABC, if a = 13, b = 14 and c = 15, then \(\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\) = ______.
items.ourVersionWrong: The stem. We hold "then sin^-1 x = ?", which names no quantity. The page prints "then \(\sin\left(\frac{A}{2}\right)\) = ______." -- a plain sin (no inverse superscript) applied to A-over-2 in large parentheses. There is no inverse sine and no x anywhere in the printed stem. Secondary difference: option B is printed as ONE radical spanning the whole fraction, \(\sqrt{1/5}\), not as \(1/\sqrt{5}\) (same value, different printed form). A, C, D are faithful. The printed stem settles the dispute in favour of the sin(A/2) reading: s = 21, sin(A/2) = sqrt((s-b)(s-c)/(bc)) = sqrt(7*6/(14*15)) = sqrt(1/5), so the key is B.
items.source: Maths 2017 paper.pdf, page index 0, Q.1(A) iii; crop y 0.485-0.590 x 0.08-0.68 @130dpi (q2_2017_iii.png)

items.printedStem: The direction ratios of the line which is perpendicular to the lines with direction ratios \(-1,\ 2,\ 2\) and \(0,\ 2,\ 1\) are ______.
items.ourVersionWrong: The stem, not the options. We hold the first direction-ratio triple as "1, 2, 2"; the page prints \(-1,\ 2,\ 2\) with an unmistakable leading minus sign (re-cropped at 300dpi on the stem tail specifically to settle this -- q2019_s3stemR2.png). All four options are transcribed faithfully. With the printed stem the cross product is \((-1,2,2)\times(0,2,1) = (2\cdot 1 - 2\cdot 2,\ 2\cdot 0 - (-1)\cdot 1,\ (-1)\cdot 2 - 2\cdot 0) = (-2,\ 1,\ -2)\), which is exactly option D. The paper is internally consistent and no option is corrupt -- the suspicion that both Q.2 and Q.3 of this paper carry a corrupt option is not borne out; both defects are ours.
items.source: Maths 2019 paper.pdf, page index 0, Q.3; crops y 0.625-0.700 x 0.03-0.80 @130dpi and y 0.626-0.645 x 0.60-1.00 @300dpi (q2019_s3.png, q2019_s3stemR2.png)

items.printedStem: The acute angle between the two planes \(x + y + 2z = 3\) and \(3x - 2y + 2z = 7\) is ______.
items.ourVersionWrong: Options A and B. We hold their numerator as 1; the page prints 5 in both. C and D are faithful (numerator 15). The printed numerator sequence is 5, 5, 15, 15 -- not 1, 1, 15, 15. Since \(\cos\theta = \frac{|n_1\cdot n_2|}{|n_1||n_2|} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{6}\,\sqrt{17}} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{102}}\), option B is the key and the paper is internally consistent. The 15/sqrt(102) pair are ordinary distractors; that they fall outside the arccos domain is a distractor artefact, not a misprint.
items.source: Maths 2019 paper.pdf, page index 0, Q.2; crop y 0.535-0.632 x 0.03-0.80 @130dpi (q2019_s2.png)

items.printedStem: If \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are direction angles of a line and \(\alpha = 60^\circ\), \(\beta = 45^\circ\), then \(\gamma\) = ______.
items.ourVersionWrong: The symbol after "then". We hold a Latin "r"; the printed symbol is a Greek GAMMA. Read at 190dpi the glyph is identical to the third symbol in the stem's own "\(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\)" list (same descender, same open top) and is clearly not a Latin r. Same mis-read class as the italic-t sibling. All four options are faithful. With the printed stem, \(\cos^2 60^\circ + \cos^2 45^\circ + \cos^2\gamma = 1 \Rightarrow \cos^2\gamma = 1/4 \Rightarrow \gamma = 60^\circ\) or \(120^\circ\) = option D, so the paper is internally consistent. Worth noting for the key: option C is printed \(130^\circ\), not \(120^\circ\).
items.source: Maths 2024 paper.pdf, page index 1 (printed Page 2), Q.1 (iii); crop y 0.420-0.545 x 0.10-0.80 @190dpi (q5_2024_iii.png)

items.ourVersionWrong: The denominator. We hold \((b+c)\); the page prints a single lowercase \(a\). At 200dpi the denominator of the middle bracket is one narrow character sitting under "b - c", with no parentheses, no plus sign and no second letter -- it cannot be read as (b+c). So the printed identity is the CORRECT Napier-type form \(\sin\frac{B-C}{2} = \frac{b-c}{a}\cos\frac{A}{2}\), and the false identity is ours alone. Note this is a 3-mark Section-C item carrying an internal OR (the alternative is "Show that \(\sin^{-1}(5/13) + \cos^{-1}(3/5) = \tan^{-1}(63/16)\)"), which we may or may not hold separately.
items.source: Maths 2019 paper.pdf, page index 1, Q.15 (Section C); crop y 0.628-0.685 x 0.05-0.45 @200dpi (q6_2019_q15b.png)

items.printedStem: If \(y = \sqrt{\sin x + \sqrt{\sin x + \sqrt{\sin x + \ldots \infty}}}\), then show that \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\cos x}{2y - 1}\)
items.ourVersionWrong: Both the leading "Evaluate:" and the trailing "dx". NEITHER is printed. The page prints the item as a bare "If y = <nested radical>, then show that dy/dx = cos x / (2y - 1)" -- it opens with "If" and ends at the fraction, with no integral sign anywhere in the item. The glue source is confirmed on the same page: the immediately preceding sibling, Q.4(B) i, reads "Evaluate: \(\int e^x\left[\frac{\sqrt{1-x^2}\cdot\sin^{-1}x + 1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\right]dx\)" -- our stem took its opening word and its closing "dx" from that neighbour. The printed question is a pure differentiation item and is correctly stated by the board; its filing under Indefinite Integration is a consequence of our own glue, not of the paper.
items.source: Maths 2015 paper.pdf, page index 2, Q.4(B) ii; crops y 0.297-0.333 x 0.08-0.72 @130dpi and (glue source) y 0.235-0.300 x 0.08-0.55 @150dpi (q7_2015_4Bii.png, q7_2015_4Bhdr.png). Q.4(A) header confirmed on page index 1 (ov2015p1bot.png).

items.ourVersionWrong: BOTH limits. The printed integral has NO limits at all -- it is an INDEFINITE integral. Read at 280dpi the integral sign stands alone with clear white space above and below it; there is no 0, no pi/2, no pi^2/4 and no exponent anywhere. So the dispute is not "pi/2 vs pi^2/4": neither is on the page. We hold a fabricated definite integral. The printed question answers to \(-2\cos\sqrt{x} + c\). Consequence for filing: this is an Indefinite Integration item, not a Definite Integration one. (Checked against the paper named in the brief; if the corpus drew this from a different sitting, that source is not in this folder.)
items.source: Maths 2017 paper.pdf, page index 2, Section II Q.4(B) iii; crop y 0.618-0.658 x 0.10-0.45 @280dpi (q8_2017_4Biii.png)

items.printedStem: Find the equation of tangent to the curve \(y = x^2 + 4x + 1\) at \((-1, -2)\).
items.ourVersionWrong: The constant term. We hold \(-1\); the page prints \(+1\). At 130dpi the sign between "4x" and "1" is a plain short horizontal bar at mid-height identical to the "+" before 4x and clearly distinct from the two minus signs in "(-1, -2)" on the same line. So the printed curve is \(y = x^2 + 4x + 1\), on which the point (-1, -2) DOES lie (1 - 4 + 1 = -2), and the paper is sound. Minor wording note: the page reads "the equation of tangent", not "the equation of the tangent".
items.source: Maths 2019 paper.pdf, page index 1, Q.12 (Section B); crop y 0.462-0.500 x 0.03-0.60 @130dpi (q9_2019_q12.png)

items.ourVersionWrong: The sign of f'(1). The page prints \(f'(1) = -\frac{1}{3}\) -- MINUS. At 260dpi a clear minus bar sits to the left of the 1-over-3 fraction, at the same height and weight as the minus signs on g(1) = -4 and g'(1) = -8/3 in the same line, and there is nothing in that position on the printed page for a plus. We hold +1/3. Options are faithful in value; note (a) is printed \(-\frac{29}{25}\) (denominator 25, not 15). With the printed minus: \(f f' + g g' = 3(-\tfrac13) + (-4)(-\tfrac83) = -1 + \tfrac{32}{3} = \tfrac{29}{3}\), and \(\sqrt{9+16} = 5\), giving \(\frac{29}{15}\) = option D. The +1/3 reading (which would give 7/3, option B) is not what the board printed.
items.source: Maths 2025 paper.pdf, page index 2 (printed Page 3), Q.1 (v); crop y 0.258-0.440 x 0.12-0.90 @260dpi (q10_2025_v.png)

items.printedStem:
The following is the p.d.f. (Probability Density Function) of a continuous random variable X:

\(f(x) = \dfrac{x}{32},\ 0 < x < 8\)

\(= 0\)  otherwise

a. Find the expression for c.d.f. (Cumulative Distribution Function) of X.
b. Also find its value at \(x = 0.5\) and 9.
items.ourVersionWrong: The numerator. The page prints a bare italic \(x\) -- NO superscript. Read at 220dpi with the crop deliberately widened upward to expose the full numerator zone, the numerator is a single italic x whose glyph and height match the two plain x's in "0 < x < 8" on the same line, and the space above it is empty white. This is not a flattened superscript: a superscript 2 in this typeface renders clearly at this dpi (compare the printed \(a^2 - x^2\) and \(x^2/1 + y^2/4\) elsewhere in the same corpus). So the printed p.d.f. is \(x/32\) on (0,8), which integrates to exactly 1, and the question is well-posed. The spurious square is ours.
items.source: Maths 2016 paper.pdf, page index 2, Q.6(B) iii; crops y 0.728-0.775 and y 0.718-0.760, x 0.10-0.38 @200/220dpi (q11_2016_6Biii.png, q11b.png)

items.printedStem:
Find the particular solution of the differential equation:

\(y(1 + \log x)\dfrac{dx}{dy} - x \log x = 0\)

when \(y = e^2\) and \(x = e\)
items.ourVersionWrong: The derivative is transposed. The page prints \(\dfrac{dx}{dy}\) -- dx above the bar, dy below. At 220dpi the numerator is unambiguously "dx" (the x is the wide italic x used throughout the line, e.g. in "log x") and the denominator is "dy" (the y carries a clear descender below the baseline). We hold dy/dx. So the printed equation separates cleanly and the board is sound; the non-elementary form is ours. Wording note: the printed initial condition is a separate line reading "when \(y = e^2\) and \(x = e\)" with no terminal full stop.
items.source: Maths 2018 paper.pdf, page index 3, Q.6(B) ii; crop y 0.676-0.725 x 0.10-0.50 @220dpi (q12_2018_6Bii.png)

section2019.source: Maths 2019 paper.pdf. Section A = Q.1-Q.6, all MCQ, 1 mark each. Q.1-Q.5 on page index 0; Q.6 at the top of page index 1, immediately above the SECTION B banner.
section2019.instruction: Select and write the most appropriate answer from the given alternative for each question:
section2019.paperNote: Note (3) on the cover: the paper has 30 questions in FOUR sections -- A (6 questions, 1 mark), B (8 x 2 marks, one with internal option), C (6 x 3 marks, two with internal options), D (10 x 4 marks, three with internal options). Note (4): for each MCQ the answer must be written with its alphabet, and for Q.1 to Q.6 only the first attempt is evaluated.

questions.stem: The principal solutions of \(\cot x = -\sqrt{3}\) are ______.
questions.check: cot x = -sqrt(3) => tan x = -1/sqrt(3) => x = 5pi/6, 11pi/6 in [0, 2pi). Matches option C exactly; no defect.

questions.stem: The acute angle between the two planes \(x + y + 2z = 3\) and \(3x - 2y + 2z = 7\) is ______.
questions.check: cos(theta) = 5/(sqrt(6)*sqrt(17)) = 5/sqrt(102). Matches option B exactly; no defect. (This is line-planes-12-pyq#32.)

questions.stem: The direction ratios of the line which is perpendicular to the lines with direction ratios \(-1,\ 2,\ 2\) and \(0,\ 2,\ 1\) are ______.
questions.check: (-1,2,2) x (0,2,1) = (-2, 1, -2). Matches option D exactly; no defect. (This is line-planes-12-pyq#2.)

questions.stem: If \(f(x) = (1 + 2x)^{\frac{1}{x}}\), for \(x \neq 0\) is continuous at \(x = 0\), then \(f(0)\) = ______.
questions.check: lim (1+2x)^(1/x) = e^2 as x -> 0. Matches option B exactly; no defect.

int dx/(9x^2+1) = (1/3) arctan(3x) + c. Matches option C exactly; no defect. Note the integrand is printed with dx in the NUMERATOR of the fraction, i.e. \(\int \frac{dx}{9x^2+1}\), not \(\int \frac{1}{9x^2+1}dx\).

questions.stem: If \(y = ae^{5x} + be^{-5x}\), then the differential equation is ______.
questions.check: y'' = 25(ae^{5x} + be^{-5x}) = 25y. Matches option A exactly; no defect.

section2019.conclusion: All six Section-A questions of the 2019 paper are internally consistent: each one's correct value is printed verbatim as one of its four options, and no option or stem on the page is defective. The two defects reported for this paper (Q.2 and Q.3) are both ours, so the suspicion that the 2019 paper itself carries two corrupt options does not survive the page. The 2019 items reported separately from Sections B and C (Q.12 tangent, Q.15 Napier identity) are likewise sound in print.
